chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the women: 'Do not prolong your Prayers in order to prevent your husbands.'

key_terms.صَلَاتَكُنَّ: Your prayers (specifically referring to the women's prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women prolonging their prayers if it affects their husbands?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the reliable chain of Abu Basir, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Prophet’s instruction to women was not a prohibition of long prayer, but a caution against excessive prolongation that neglects conjugal rights. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing individual devotion with social and marital duties, ensuring that worship does not become a source of friction within the family unit.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to the women: ‘Do not prolong your Prayers in order to prevent your husbands’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from abu al-Mighra’ from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said to women, ‘You must not prolong your Salat (prayer) to prevent your husbands.’”
